review::.::holistic::cross_module_archit.summary: The Workspace generation_lock publication protocol is honored by the LSP transport only; daemon dispatchers query and mutate without it

evidence: crates/al-workspace/src/lib.rs:152-158 documents generation_lock as the workspace-wide publication contract: "LSP request handlers hold a read guard while querying; a reindex holds the write guard only for the final in-memory swap."

Every acquisition of generation_lock in the repository is in crates/al-lsp/src/server/{lsp.rs,workspace.rs,diagnostics.rs}. No file under crates/al-lsp/src/server/daemon/ acquires it, in either direction.

crates/al-lsp/src/server/daemon/build_dispatch/build/file_refresh.rs:156-174 and :261-278 publish in-memory mutations (documents.replace_or_open / rename, file_index.add_file / remove_file, invalidate_insight_graph) and bump the revision via mark_generation_changed, but never take the write guard, while crates/al-lsp/src/server/daemon/mod.rs serves up to MAX_CONNECTIONS = 64 concurrent requests.

The daemon substitutes an unrelated protocol — project_state_with_wait at crates/al-lsp/src/server/daemon/mod.rs:1002-1031 wraps a 500ms LOCK_WAIT timeout in block_in_place/block_on and returns "Project state is busy (configuration reload or reindex in progress); retry the request".

The same query is reached both ways with different readiness discipline: crates/al-lsp/src/server/lsp.rs:1606-1624 (hover) calls snapshot_after_ready, ensure_builtins_loaded and re-checks snapshot_is_current, while dispatch_hover in crates/al-lsp/src/server/daemon/lsp_dispatch.rs does only ensure_document before calling the same al_analysis::queries::hover::hover_full.
detail.suggestion: Move the guard into al-workspace so it cannot be transport-specific: wrap the file_refresh mutations in a `Workspace::publish_generation(|| ...)` helper that takes the write guard and bumps the revision in one place, and have the daemon's query dispatchers take the read guard the same way the LSP handlers do. If the daemon deliberately opts out, say so in the generation_lock doc comment on crates/al-workspace/src/lib.rs:152 rather than leaving the field's stated contract false for one of its two callers.

review::.::holistic::cross_module_archit.summary: Workspace exposes ~20 public locked fields that consumer crates mutate directly, leaving its lock invariants as prose

review::.::holistic::convention_outlier:.summary: al-explorer pins edition 2024 while all 20 sibling crates inherit 2021, creating a formatting and semantics island

evidence: crates/al-explorer/Cargo.toml line 4 is `edition = "2024"`. Every other crate manifest says `edition.workspace = true`, and [workspace.package] in the root Cargo.toml sets edition = "2021". No comment in the manifest explains the pin.

Rustfmt's style edition follows the crate edition, so the pin changes use-tree sorting. al-explorer: `use crate::{App, MAX_INPUT_LEN, advance_list_selection, ensure_daemon_client, input_focused_style};` (views/call_graph.rs:12) and `use crate::{ActivePane, App, ClickTarget, MAX_INPUT_LEN, display_object_id, pad_center, pane_style, truncate_with_ellipsis};` (views/object_browser.rs:10) put uppercase items before lowercase ones.

Everywhere else the ordering is the opposite: `use al_protocol::jsonrpc::{error_codes, Response};`, `use al_syntax::context::{detect_context, CompletionContext};`, `use crate::queries::tests::{collect_test_procedures, TestCodeunit};`, `pub use lsp::{run_lsp, AlServer};`. A grep for the uppercase-first ordering across al-analysis, al-lsp and al-symbols returned zero matches, so the split is exactly at the al-explorer boundary.

The edition also changes language semantics for this one crate (match ergonomics, unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn, tail-expression temporary drop scope), so an idiom copied from a sibling crate can behave differently here — relevant given crates/al-explorer/src/main.rs already contains an `unsafe` libc::signal block.
detail.suggestion: Either change crates/al-explorer/Cargo.toml to `edition.workspace = true` and run `cargo fmt -p al-explorer` to bring its imports back in line, or, if edition 2024 is deliberate (for example to pick up a specific ratatui/crossterm idiom), record the reason in a comment above the key and add `style_edition = "2024"` to a workspace rustfmt.toml so the whole workspace formats the same way. review::.::holistic::error_consistency::.summary: bulk_fix::collect_al_files is a pass-through that only erases ScanError, and its al-lsp callers map the String to INTERNAL_ERROR

review::.::holistic::error_consistency::.summary: hover_full, completions_full and load_profile_file stringify typed errors inside al-analysis, before any caller can match on them

review::.::holistic::naming_quality::sho.summary: `should_report_semantic_failure(&self) -> bool` reads as a predicate but performs an atomic swap

review::.::holistic::naming_quality::ser.summary: `default_900` and `default_5` name the value rather than what it configures

review::.::holistic::naming_quality::thr.summary: AlFormatConfig, FormattingConfig and FormatOptions all hold formatting settings and the names do not say which layer each is

review::.::holistic::naming_quality::sym.summary: SymbolIndex encodes one-vs-many in get_ vs find_ without documenting it, and al-source spells the same lookups with no verb

evidence: index.rs:1041 `get_by_name(&self, name) -> Vec<Arc<SymbolEntry>>` and index.rs:1051 `find_by_name(&self, name) -> Option<Arc<SymbolEntry>>` differ only in verb; nothing in the module docs states that get_ means all matches and find_ means the first.

file_index.rs:629/648/679 solves the same problem with object_path -> Option, object_paths -> Vec and find_by_object_name -> Option, so a developer moving between the two crates meets three spellings of one idea.

review::.::holistic::naming_quality::tes.summary: 621 of 4280 tests carry a redundant `test_` prefix and 32 files mix both naming styles internally

review::.::holistic::naming_quality::mcp.summary: `obj_schema` builds MCP tool input schemas but is the only name in its group that abbreviates and omits its role

review::.::holistic::naming_quality::exp.summary: al-explorer CLI printers bind extracted JSON fields to two-letter names where the same file elsewhere spells them out

evidence: insight.rs:419-421 binds `so` and `sm` for a subscriber's objectName and methodName; :433-439 binds `oo`, `om` and `te` for an orphan subscriber's objectName, methodName and targetEvent, printed as `{oo}.{om} -> {to}::{te}`.

review::.::holistic::abstraction_fitness.summary: 26-field `Workspace` god-struct is threaded into 145 al-analysis query signatures that use three of its fields

evidence: al-workspace/src/lib.rs:143 `pub struct Workspace` declares 26 fields (20 public) covering DocumentStore, SymbolIndex, toolchain, AlProject, the .NET semantic bridge, merged AlConfig, builtins, compiler error codes, a native debug session, profiler session, test results, four lazily-built graph caches and six lock/counter primitives.
145 function signatures across 45 files in crates/al-analysis/src take `&Workspace`.

Counting field accesses across al-analysis: file_index 145, documents 94, symbols 91, get_or_build_call_graph 12, profiler_session 10, config 7, generation_revision 3, test_results 2, builtins 2 — roughly 10 of the 26 members are ever reached, and three account for the bulk.

Consequence: `queries::definition::definition(&Workspace, uri, pos)` is handed the live debug session and profiler state, so a reader cannot tell from a signature what state a query depends on, and a query cannot be exercised without constructing the whole server.
detail.suggestion: Introduce a narrow read-side view — e.g. `pub struct SourceSnapshot<'a> { documents: &'a DocumentStore, symbols: &'a SymbolIndex, file_index: &'a FileIndex }` in al-workspace, with `Workspace::snapshot(&self) -> SourceSnapshot<'_>` — and change the al-analysis query signatures to take it. The handful of queries that genuinely need more (code_lens reads profiler_session, impact reads the call graph) keep `&Workspace`, which then documents itself as the exception. This removes a parameter's worth of reach rather than adding a layer: no new trait, no new crate, one struct.

review::.::holistic::abstraction_fitness.summary: Daemon JSON-RPC payloads have no typed structs in either direction; 131 hand-rolled extractors and 534 `.get("field")` reads stand in

evidence: Inbound: daemon/mod.rs:852-905 defines `extract_uri`, `extract_position`, `extract_i32`, `optional_bool_param`, `optional_bounded_usize_param`, each pulling one field out of `&serde_json::Value`. These are used at 131 call sites across crates/al-lsp/src/server/daemon/, against 5 uses of `serde_json::from_value` in the same directory.

Outbound: lsp_dispatch.rs:18 `fn ok_response<T: Serialize>` proves the daemon already holds typed results, but al-explorer/src/cli/commands/mod.rs:425 `request_checked` returns `serde_json::Value`, and the CLI re-derives every shape by hand — 534 `.get("...")` sites across al-explorer, e.g. lsp/query.rs:31-40 reads kind/id/name/package/source_availability out of a map with `.unwrap_or("?")` fallbacks.

al-protocol carries only the JSON-RPC envelope and socket transport (lib.rs exports DaemonClient, jsonrpc, socket) and al-types already exists as the shared tier-0 crate, so a home for the payload types is present and unused.
detail.suggestion: Move the request/response payload structs for the highest-traffic daemon methods into al-protocol (or al-types) as plain `#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]` types, have the dispatchers take `serde_json::from_value::<HoverParams>(params)` instead of `extract_uri`+`extract_position`, and have al-explorer deserialize into the same structs instead of `.get("...")`. Start with the ~20 lsp_dispatch methods, which share the uri+position shape. This is a net deletion: the extractor helpers, most of the `.get` chains, and most of response_contract.rs go away.

review::.::holistic::abstraction_fitness.summary: 1451-line hand-maintained runtime schema validator compensates for the missing typed response structs, and covers only 60 of 84 daemon methods

evidence: response_contract.rs is 1451 lines whose module doc states the motive: "The daemon is a separate process and JSON-RPC is an untyped boundary. Human formatters must not turn a missing field into `0`, `false`, `?`, or an empty list and then exit successfully."
It re-implements a type system: a private `enum Kind { String, Integer, Unsigned, Number, Boolean, Array, Object }` with `matches(&Value)` and a `label()` for error text (lines 10-44).

`handles(method)` (line 46) enumerates ~60 method names; daemon/mod.rs dispatches 84. The uncovered remainder falls through to a second ad-hoc validator, `validate_run_command_result` (al-explorer/src/cli/commands/mod.rs:440), so the guarantee is partial and the split is invisible at the call site.
Every field named in this validator is a field that a `#[derive(Deserialize)]` struct would check at the parse boundary for free.
detail.suggestion: Fold this into the typed-payload fix above: once al-explorer deserializes daemon results into shared structs, serde's missing-field and type errors replace the Kind/label machinery, and `request_checked` becomes `client.request::<T>(method, params)`. Retire response_contract.rs and validate_run_command_result together rather than extending either — the current pair has to be updated by hand every time a daemon response gains a field.

review::.::holistic::abstraction_fitness.summary: Canonical `al_types::jsonc` helper is reimplemented in two crates and reached through a 7-line re-export facade in al-dap

evidence: al-types/src/jsonc.rs (204 lines) defines `strip_json_comments` and `strip_trailing_commas` as the shared implementation; al-bc/src/launch.rs:8 uses it correctly.
al-project/src/config.rs:759 defines a private `fn strip_jsonc(source: &str) -> String` that walks the same in_string/escaped state machine again.
al-lsp/src/server/workspace.rs:1454 defines a third copy, `strip_jsonc_comments_and_parse`, with the same in_string/escape_next loop.

That same al-lsp function then calls `al_dap::dap::json_util::strip_trailing_commas` at line 1524, so the language server depends on the debug-adapter crate for a string utility that lives in al-types.

al-dap/src/dap/json_util.rs is 7 lines: a doc comment saying "The canonical implementations now live in the tier-0 `al-types` crate; this module re-exports them so existing `crate::dap::json_util::…` paths keep working" plus one `pub use`. It defines no logic of its own and is now load-bearing for a crate outside al-dap.
detail.suggestion: Delete al-dap/src/dap/json_util.rs and rewrite its in-crate references plus al-lsp/src/server/workspace.rs:1524 to `al_types::jsonc::strip_trailing_commas`. Replace `strip_jsonc_comments_and_parse` (workspace.rs:1454) and `strip_jsonc` (config.rs:759) with `serde_json::from_str(&strip_trailing_commas(&strip_json_comments(&source)))`, keeping the workspace.rs regression tests at lines 1613-1680 pointed at the shared helper. Three implementations and a facade collapse to one call.

review::.::holistic::abstraction_fitness.summary: MockRecord carries 20 pure pass-through methods forwarding to its `_in(view, ...)` variants, with no production caller

evidence: record.rs defines each table operation twice: `get_in`/`get`, `insert_in`/`insert`, `modify_in`/`modify`, `delete_in`/`delete`, `delete_all_in`/`delete_all`, `rename_in`/`rename`, `set_filter_in`/`set_filter`, `find_first_in`/`find_first`, `find_last_in`/`find_last`, `find_set_in`/`find_set`, `find_in`/`find`, `next_in`/`next`, `count_in`/`count`, `is_empty_in`/`is_empty`, `init_in`/`init`, `reset_in`/`reset`.

Every short-named method has a one-line body of the identical form, e.g. line 367 `pub fn get(&mut self, key: PrimaryKey) -> Result<(), RecordError> { self.with_default_view(|table, view| table.get_in(view, key)) }`.

Scanning every MockRecord call site: crates/al-runtime/src/interpreter/{records,eval_stmt,value}.rs — the only production consumers — use the `_in` forms exclusively (get_in, insert_in, modify_in, delete_in, find_first_in, next_in, count_in, is_empty_in, set_range_in, set_filter_in, ...). No production call reaches a default-view method.
The only callers of the short forms are record.rs's own `mod tests` (line 888 onward) and crates/al-test/benches/interpreter.rs:177-246.
detail.suggestion: Delete the 20 default-view methods and `with_default_view`, and move the default `RecordView` into the test/bench setup instead: a `fn make_table() -> (MockRecord, RecordView)` helper in record.rs's test module and the same two lines in benches/interpreter.rs. Tests then exercise the same entry points production uses, and the public surface of MockRecord halves.

review::.::holistic::abstraction_fitness.summary: al-lsp's per-feature handler-module seam is used for five LSP features and bypassed for five others inlined into lsp.rs

evidence: Features routed through a handler module: hover (lsp.rs:1614 -> server/hover.rs), completion (1633 -> server/completions.rs), goto_definition (1659 -> server/definition.rs), rename and prepare_rename (-> definition.rs:71,87), formatting (-> server/formatting.rs).
Features calling al_analysis inline from lsp.rs instead: goto_implementation (1679), references (1715), document_symbol (1755), semantic_tokens_full (1834), code_lens (2052).

definition.rs:68 records the drift explicitly: "handle_references was inlined into the LanguageServer::references impl and wrapped in spawn_blocking so it can be cancel-friendly. Removed." The stated reason (spawn_blocking) is orthogonal to where the conversion lives.
detail.suggestion: Pick one shape and apply it to all ten. The cheaper direction is to finish inlining: move the four handler-module bodies into their `LanguageServer` methods in lsp.rs, keeping `origin_selection_range` and `core_workspace_edit_to_lsp` as free functions in server/handlers.rs, and delete hover.rs, definition.rs and completions.rs. review::.::holistic::abstraction_fitness.summary: Public default-argument wrappers in al-insight and al-symbols forward to the real function with `None` and have only test callers

evidence: search.rs:503 `pub fn find_entry_points(graph: &InsightGraph) -> Vec<&InsightNode> { find_entry_points_with_calls(graph, None) }`, and its own doc at :498-502 warns that without a call graph the variant "reports nearly every procedure" and says "Prefer find_entry_points_with_calls, which is what the entrypoints command uses".
search.rs:52 `pub fn trace_event(graph, event_name, max_depth) { trace_event_with_calls(graph, None, event_name, max_depth) }`, doc at :48-51 again points callers at the `_with_calls` form.
nuget.rs:90 `pub fn resolve_dependencies(deps: &[AppDependency]) -> Vec<PackageRef> { resolve_dependencies_for_country(deps, None) }`.

Production uses the full forms: al-lsp/src/server/daemon/insight_dispatch.rs:53 and :70. Every caller of the three wrappers is a test in the same file (search.rs:727,763,791,847,1291,1334,1411; calls.rs:2610,2657; nuget.rs:849-1098) or al-lsp/benches/perf.rs:422.
The wrappers are public and their names read as the primary API, so a new caller reaching for the obvious name silently gets the degraded analysis the doc comment warns about.
detail.suggestion: Delete the three wrappers and pass `None` explicitly at the test and bench call sites, which is one extra argument per call and makes the degraded mode visible where it is chosen. If a short name is wanted, rename `find_entry_points_with_calls` to `find_entry_points` taking `Option<&CallGraph>` so there is one spelling.

review::.::holistic::abstraction_fitness.summary: RunOptions passes 7 fields through the TestSession interface; implementors read 3 and the other 3 are consumed by the caller that built it

evidence: session.rs:29 `RunOptions` declares timeout_ms, parallel, junit_out, cobertura_out, filter, coverage (7 fields with the serde default), and session.rs:128 `TestSession::run(&self, tests, opts: RunOptions, tx)` takes it whole.
Both implementors read only three fields: interp.rs:156,173,210 and live_bc.rs:226,231,287 use timeout_ms, filter and parallel.

junit_out, cobertura_out and coverage are never read inside al-test; the only reads are in the module that constructs the struct — tests_dispatch.rs:885,901 (`if opts.coverage`) and :1085,1094 (report paths).
The effect is that the run interface advertises report-writing and coverage as part of the backend contract when they are the dispatcher's own concerns.

Coverage already selects a constructor rather than a runtime branch (`InterpMode::with_coverage`), so tests_dispatch.rs can keep that decision locally, and the two report paths belong beside the code that writes the reports. RunOptions then shrinks to the three fields the trait actually contracts for.

review::.::holistic::dependency_health::.summary: al-lsp declares 14 production dependencies its source never references, residue from the crate split

evidence: grep for `use <name>` and `<name>::` across crates/al-lsp (src, tests, benches, examples) returns zero hits for al-publish, dashmap, ropey, tree-sitter-al, urlencoding, petgraph, tokio-tungstenite, futures-util, quick-xml, memmap2, rayon, getrandom, zeroize and keyring.

Each is already in the build graph through the crate that actually uses it (dashmap/ropey via al-source, petgraph via al-insight, quick-xml/memmap2/rayon/keyring/zeroize via al-symbols, tokio-tungstenite/futures-util via al-dap, tree-sitter-al via al-syntax), so nothing is lost and the duplicated keyring and tokio-tungstenite feature blocks stop being a second place to keep in sync. While there, delete `rayon` from al-analysis, `url` from al-bc, and `al-project` + `al-types` from al-publish, which are unused by the same check.

review::.::holistic::dependency_health::.summary: Ten shared crates including tree-sitter and url are pinned per-manifest instead of in [workspace.dependencies]

evidence: The workspace table already carries 22 crates with `{ workspace = true }` used consistently for serde, tokio, thiserror, zip, quick-xml and the rest, so the mechanism exists and is understood.

Outside it: tree-sitter = "0.25" is repeated in 9 manifests (al-types, al-syntax, al-source, al-analysis, al-insight, al-emit, al-runtime, al-test, al-lsp), url = "2" in 8, tempfile = "3" in 14, dirs = "6" in 4, sha2 = "0.10" in 3, rayon = "1" in 3, urlencoding = "2" in 3.

The url pins have already diverged: crates/al-analysis/Cargo.toml:24 is `url = { version = "2", features = ["serde"] }` while the other seven are bare `url = "2"`, so whether Url serializes depends on Cargo feature unification rather than on any crate's own declaration.

Both types cross public crate boundaries: crates/al-types/src/procedure.rs:12 returns `Option<(String, tree_sitter::Tree)>` from a trait method and crates/al-workspace/src/lib.rs:918 takes `&url::Url`. If one manifest is bumped to tree-sitter 0.26 and the others are not, Cargo resolves two copies and the trait no longer matches its implementors.
detail.suggestion: Move tree-sitter, url (with features = ["serde"], which al-analysis already needs), tempfile, dirs, sha2, rayon and urlencoding into [workspace.dependencies] in the root Cargo.toml and replace each per-crate pin with `{ workspace = true }`, matching how serde and tokio are already handled. This removes about 40 duplicate lines and makes a version bump a one-line edit that cannot leave a crate behind.

review::.::holistic::dependency_health::.summary: al-symbols uses the futures umbrella crate while al-dap uses futures-util for the same combinators

evidence: crates/al-symbols/src/bc_server.rs:340 and crates/al-symbols/src/nuget.rs:317 call futures::future::join_all, backed by the workspace `futures = "0.3"` entry.
crates/al-dap/src/dap/bc_debug/session.rs:8 imports futures_util::{SinkExt, StreamExt}, backed by a separate `futures-util = "0.3"` pin in al-dap and a duplicate one in al-lsp.
`futures` re-exports futures-util, so both crates end up in the graph and a reader cannot tell from a manifest which facade a new async call site is supposed to use.
Total first-party usage is four call sites: one join_all pair and one SinkExt/StreamExt import.
detail.suggestion: Pick futures-util and use it everywhere: it is the crate both actually need, and dropping `futures` removes futures-executor and futures-channel from the graph. Change al-symbols' two call sites to futures_util::future::join_all, delete the `futures` entry from [workspace.dependencies] and from al-symbols and al-lsp, and add futures-util to [workspace.dependencies] so al-dap and any future consumer share one pin.

review::.::holistic::dependency_health::.summary: Workspace pins getrandom 0.2 on the deprecated API while the lock already builds 0.3.4 and 0.4.2

evidence: Cargo.toml declares `getrandom = "0.2"` in [workspace.dependencies].
Cargo.lock contains getrandom 0.2.17, 0.3.4 and 0.4.2; 0.3.4 arrives via quinn-proto, jobserver and zip 2.4.2, and 0.4.2 via tempfile 3.27 and uuid. The first-party pin is the oldest of the three.

All three first-party call sites use the free function removed after 0.2: crates/al-emit/src/package.rs:44 and :53, crates/al-symbols/src/oauth.rs:589, crates/al-runtime/src/stubs/any.rs:225 all call `getrandom::getrandom(&mut buf)`, which is `getrandom::fill` from 0.3 onward.
Each site fills a fixed-size byte buffer for a GUID or an OAuth PKCE verifier, so the migration is a name change at four lines with no behavioral difference.

review::.::holistic::dependency_health::.summary: CI enforces licenses and advisories but nothing detects unused dependencies, so dead entries accumulate

evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:145-161 runs cargo-deny --workspace, and deny.toml covers [licenses], [advisories] and [bans]. None of those categories reports a declared-but-unreferenced dependency.
The Makefile's only manifest-related check (line 333, 'local package-manifest audit for publishable crates') validates publish metadata, not dependency use.

The gap is measurable: 17 unused production entries survive across crates/al-lsp (14), al-analysis (1), al-bc (1) and al-publish (2), with al-lsp's dating back to the manifests copied during the crate split.
detail.suggestion: Add a cargo-machete step to the existing cargo-deny job in .github/workflows/ci.yml. It needs no config file, runs in seconds, and would have caught all 17 entries. cargo-udeps is the alternative but needs nightly, so machete is the cheaper fit for this workspace.

review::.::holistic::low_level_elegance:.summary: optional_non_empty_string is copy-pasted into three daemon dispatch modules and the third copy reports a different error

evidence: debug_dispatch.rs:77-95 and build_dispatch/tests_dispatch.rs:19-37 are byte-identical match-based implementations of `fn optional_non_empty_string<'a>(params: &serde_json::Value, key: &str) -> Result<Option<&'a str>, String>`.

review::.::holistic::test_strategy::tui_.summary: The only TUI test adapts its assertions to whichever daemon a prior test left resident

review::.::holistic::authorization_consi.summary: env-token-then-OAuth precedence is copy-pasted at four dispatch sites; only bc_server recovers from a 401

review::.::holistic::authorization_consi.summary: Sibling daemon methods use 'must be absolute' as a path-traversal guard while one uses real containment

evidence: 38 sibling .rs files plus one child directory (code_actions), the largest flat directory in the workspace
Eleven are per-request LSP features, seven are lint families, seven are batch reporting tools that run over a whole project rather than a cursor position
The three groups have different lifetimes and different callers: LSP features answer one editor request, lints run over a file set, reports run over a project
detail.suggestion: Move the files into queries/lsp/, queries/lint/ and queries/report/ alongside the existing code_actions/. This is a pure move with mod.rs path updates; it does not change any signature.

review::.::holistic::package_organizatio.summary: lib.rs is a thin manifest in 15 crates and the whole implementation in 4

evidence: crates/al-compile/src/lib.rs is 1695 LOC and the crate's only source file; crates/al-publish/src/lib.rs is 869 LOC and likewise
crates/al-workspace/src/lib.rs is 1865 LOC of implementation while the crate has three other files
In the other 15 crates lib.rs is a short module list with a //! header
detail.suggestion: Split the four outliers so lib.rs is a module manifest everywhere: al-compile into its build phases, al-publish into upload and install, al-workspace's state accessors out of lib.rs. The convention already exists in 15 crates, so this makes the layout predictable rather than adding a new rule.

review::.::holistic::package_organizatio.summary: al-analysis carries 20 percent of the workspace in one crate

evidence: 46,858 LOC across 57 files, against 31,447 for al-lsp and 20,497 for al-runtime
It owns the query engine, AL type resolution, XLIFF translation handling, permissions and scaffolding, which are separate change boundaries with separate callers
xliff.rs alone is 2363 LOC and has nothing to do with the LSP query path
detail.suggestion: Move the XLIFF translation code (xliff.rs and its callers) into its own crate; it is a self-contained file-format concern that the query engine does not use. Leave the rest, whose coupling to the query path is real.

review::.::holistic::initialization_coup.summary: al-syntax and al-symbols each hold an independent LazyLock snapshot of object_types.json, with different struct shapes

evidence: crates/al-syntax/src/language_data.rs:160 loads OBJECT_TYPES through the tree_sitter_al::data accessor
crates/al-symbols/src/language_data.rs:29 loads the same file through include_str!("../../../tree-sitter-al/data/object_types.json"), a raw path reaching three directories out of the crate
The two ObjectType structs differ, so a field added to the JSON reaches one consumer and not the other with no compile error
detail.suggestion: Delete crates/al-symbols/src/language_data.rs and use al_syntax::language_data, which al-symbols already depends on per crates/al-symbols/Cargo.toml:10. One loader, one struct, one snapshot.

review::.::holistic::initialization_coup.summary: Two daemon-wide OnceLocks are set at boot and read everywhere with no defined behaviour if a caller runs before boot

evidence: DAEMON_EPOCH (line 43) and SOCKET_PATH (line 52) are process-wide OnceLocks initialised during daemon startup
Readers across the daemon assume initialisation has already happened, which holds for the real boot path but is an undocumented ordering assumption for tests and for the in-process MCP path
detail.suggestion: Document on each static which startup step sets it, and have the readers state the fallback they take when it is unset rather than leaving it implicit.

review::.::holistic::design_coherence::d.summary: The daemon's 84 RPC methods each hand-write the same decode-and-assemble block, producing the workspace's five longest functions

evidence: dispatch_tests_run_batch is 636 lines and dispatch_debug 599 (lines 242-841), both dominated by sequential parameter extraction and response construction
131 hand-rolled extract_* calls across the daemon against 5 serde_json::from_value uses; zero Deserialize derives across the ~90 methods
A separate 1451-line response_contract.rs restates the response shapes for 60 of the 84 methods
detail.suggestion: Give each method a #[derive(Deserialize)] params struct and let serde do the extraction. That deletes the extract_* calls, shrinks the dispatchers to their actual logic, and makes response_contract.rs largely redundant, so it removes code rather than adding a layer.

review::.::holistic::design_coherence::h.summary: Thirty-seven production functions take more than six parameters, topping out at eleven

evidence: crates/al-analysis/src/queries/code_lens.rs::record_file takes 11 parameters
insert_object_groups (al-emit/symbol_reference.rs), collect_coverage_from_tree (queries/test_coverage.rs) and trace_from_node (queries/suggest_event.rs) each take 10
These are internal recursion helpers threading accumulated state down a tree walk
detail.suggestion: For the tree-walk helpers, group only the parameters that are genuinely one thing: the accumulated output buffers. Leave the position and node arguments separate, since grouping those would hide what varies per call.

review::.::holistic::design_coherence::w.summary: A 26-field Workspace struct is threaded through 145 signatures that touch about ten of its members

evidence: crates/al-workspace/src/lib.rs defines Workspace with 26 fields, roughly 20 of them public and lock-wrapped
About 145 al-analysis signatures take &Workspace; collectively they read around ten members, three of which dominate
Roughly 100 lock acquisitions on those public fields happen outside the crate that owns them
detail.suggestion: Keep the &Workspace parameter but make the fields private and expose the three dominant accessors as methods, so the locking discipline lives with the data instead of at 100 external call sites.

review::.::holistic::contract_coherence:.summary: simple_error means two different return types in sibling modules of one crate

evidence: dispatch.rs:1146 defines fn simple_error(msg: impl Into<String>) -> Eval, wrapping the error in Eval::Error
eval_expr.rs:154 and eval_stmt.rs:1185 both define fn simple_error(...) -> ErrorInfo
All three live in crates/al-runtime/src/interpreter, so a reader moving between the files gets a different type from the same call
detail.suggestion: Keep one ErrorInfo-returning simple_error as pub(crate) in interpreter/mod.rs, and rename the dispatch.rs variant to eval_error to say what it wraps. Two names, two types, no ambiguity.

review::.::holistic::contract_coherence:.summary: A module's stated reason for existing is contradicted by its own Cargo.toml

evidence: The module doc at line 3 says symbols cannot depend on syntax and that this is why it loads data files directly
crates/al-symbols/Cargo.toml:10 declares al-syntax = { path = "../al-syntax", version = "0.1.0" }
The claim is the sole justification for a duplicated loader and a narrower ObjectType struct
detail.suggestion: Delete the module and use al_syntax::language_data. If the dependency rule is meant to be reinstated, remove the al-syntax dependency from the manifest instead, but the two cannot both stand.

review::.::holistic::contract_coherence:.summary: A one-line pass-through erases a typed error, collapsing two different failures into one editor message

evidence: bulk_fix.rs:154 forwards to the al-source scan and maps ScanError to String, adding nothing else
ScanError distinguishes FileTooLarge { path, size, limit } from I/O failure
The four al-lsp call sites map the resulting String to INTERNAL_ERROR, so a user who hit a configurable file limit sees the same thing as a disk fault
detail.suggestion: Delete the wrapper and let the caller handle ScanError directly, mapping FileTooLarge to an actionable message and the I/O variants to INTERNAL_ERROR.

review::.::holistic::contract_coherence:.summary: 177 Result<_, String> signatures sit beside thiserror enums, eight modules using both conventions in one file

evidence: 177 Result<_, String> signatures across crates/*/src, concentrated in al-analysis/src/queries (bulk_fix.rs alone has 19) and al-explorer's CLI
crates/al-analysis/src/queries/hover.rs:16 returns a typed error while hover.rs:325 returns Result<_, String>
The split follows neither layer nor risk: bulk_fix.rs performs the on-disk mutation with String errors while read-only query modules are typed
detail.suggestion: Convert the al-analysis/src/queries String errors to the module's existing thiserror enums, starting with bulk_fix.rs since it is the write path. The enums already exist, so this replaces format! calls with variants rather than introducing a new type.

review::.::holistic::logic_clarity::inte.summary: Roughly 194 boundary mappings collapse a typed error taxonomy into a single opaque code

evidence: About 194 sites map a query error to INTERNAL_ERROR, discarding which failure occurred
crates/al-lsp/src/server/daemon/build/metrics.rs:131 demonstrates the variant-to-code mapping working, so the pattern exists and is simply not applied at the other sites
A reader at the call site cannot tell whether the operation hit a file limit, a parse failure or a disk fault
detail.suggestion: Extend the existing variant-to-code mapping from build/metrics.rs to the other boundary sites, starting with the cases where the typed error is still in scope and is simply stringified.

review::.::holistic::logic_clarity::empt.summary: A query returns an empty result both for 'no matches' and for 'document not open'

evidence: find_implementations returns an empty Vec when the document has not been opened, the same value it returns when the symbol genuinely has no implementations
Callers cannot distinguish the two, so a missing document surfaces to the user as a confident 'no implementations'
detail.suggestion: Return Option<Vec<_>> or a typed error for the not-open case so the caller can say which happened. The distinction already matters to the editor UI.

review::.::holistic::type_safety::untype.summary: The 84-method daemon protocol has no derived types in either direction, so every payload shape is restated by hand three times

evidence: Zero Deserialize derives across roughly 90 daemon methods; 131 hand-rolled extract_* calls against 5 serde_json::from_value
The client side reads responses with about 504 raw .get("field") calls against 2 from_value sites
response_contract.rs is 1451 hand-maintained lines validating 60 of 84 methods at runtime
The same payload contract is therefore stated in the daemon's extractors, the contract validator and the MCP JSON schemas, with nothing keeping the three in step
detail.suggestion: Define a #[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)] struct per method in the shared al-protocol crate and use it on both sides. The compiler then enforces what response_contract.rs checks at runtime, so that file mostly goes away: this removes roughly 1500 lines rather than adding a layer.

review::.::holistic::type_safety::closed.summary: AL object kinds are carried as bare String on public structs although the closed set already exists as typed data

evidence: pub kind: String and pub object_type: String appear at crates/al-emit/src/symbol_extract.rs:46, :62 and :83, crates/al-explorer/src/types.rs:139, crates/al-analysis/src/xliff.rs:64, crates/al-analysis/src/permissions.rs:17 and crates/al-source/src/file_index.rs:115 and :129
crates/al-analysis/src/xliff.rs:836 constructs object_type: String::new() with the comment that it is reconstructed from the id, so the field is knowingly empty on one path
The AL object-type set is closed and already enumerated in object_types.json, loaded into typed ObjectType values by crates/al-syntax/src/language_data.rs
detail.suggestion: Replace the String fields with the existing ObjectType-derived enum in the crates that already depend on al-syntax. Where a value is genuinely absent, as at xliff.rs:836, make it Option so the empty case is visible in the type.

review::.::holistic::type_safety::string.summary: 177 Result<_, String> signatures discard error variants that thiserror enums in the same modules already define

evidence: 177 Result<_, String> signatures across crates/*/src, led by response_contract.rs (45), bulk_fix.rs (19), al-explorer cli/commands/mod.rs (12) and al-protocol client.rs (11)
The same modules define thiserror enums, so the typed variant exists and is thrown away at the signature
Downstream this forces the roughly 194 INTERNAL_ERROR mappings, because by then the variant is gone
detail.suggestion: Change the signatures to the enum that already exists in each module. The conversion is mechanical and the #[from] impls are largely in place.
